subject: Science
unitTitle: Living Organisms, Their Structure and Processes
source: El-Moasser Science Main Book 2027 + Assessments + Final Revision + Final Exams

questions.text: Organisms that make their own food are called ______.
questions.answer: autotrophs

questions.text: Organisms that depend directly or indirectly on other organisms for food are ______.
questions.answer: heterotrophs

questions.text: The process by which green plants make food in the presence of light is ______.
questions.answer: photosynthesis

questions.text: The breakdown of glucose to release energy in cells is cellular ______.
questions.answer: respiration

questions.text: Give a reason: Green algae are producers.
questions.answer: They can make their own food by photosynthesis.

questions.text: Give a reason: Rabbits are heterotrophs.
questions.answer: They depend on other organisms to obtain food.

questions.text: Compare photosynthesis and cellular respiration.
questions.answer: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, uses water and carbon dioxide and stores light energy in glucose while releasing oxygen; cellular respiration occurs in mitochondria, uses glucose and oxygen and releases energy, producing water and carbon dioxide.

questions.text: Plant pores controlled by guard cells are called ______.
questions.answer: stomata

questions.text: Give a reason: Guard cells are important.
questions.answer: They control opening and closing of stomata, helping regulate gas exchange and water vapor loss.

questions.text: Which tissue transports water and mineral salts from roots?
questions.answer: Xylem tissue

questions.text: Which tissue transports food produced in leaves?
questions.answer: Phloem tissue

questions.text: Give a reason: Blood flows through the human circulatory system in a closed cycle.
questions.answer: The heart and blood vessels are connected in a closed loop that returns blood to the heart.

questions.text: Give a reason: Food passage through the digestive system is not a closed path.
questions.answer: Food enters through the mouth and undigested wastes leave through the anus.

questions.text: Elimination of metabolic wastes is called ______.
questions.answer: excretion

questions.text: Give a reason: Kidney failure may require continuous dialysis.
questions.answer: Dialysis purifies blood from toxins, excess water, salts and urea when kidneys do not work properly.

questions.text: Give a reason: Excretion occurs in plants although they lack specialized excretory organs.
questions.answer: Leaves and stomata can eliminate excess water vapor and carbon dioxide.

questions.text: Compare autotrophs and heterotrophs.
questions.answer: Autotrophs produce their own food; heterotrophs depend on other organisms for food.

questions.text: Compare transport by xylem and phloem.
questions.answer: Xylem transports water and mineral salts from roots upward; phloem transports food made by photosynthesis from leaves to the rest of the plant.

questions.text: What happens if chloroplasts disappear from plant cells?
questions.answer: Photosynthesis stops, so the plant cannot make its own food and may die.

questions.text: What happens if the tracheal tubes in insects become blocked?
questions.answer: The insect cannot respire properly and may die.

questions.text: What happens if the phloem tissue disappears from a plant stem?
questions.answer: Food produced in leaves will not be transported to roots and other parts, leading to plant death.

questions.text: Which human organ is a main excretory organ?
questions.answer: Kidney

questions.text: Plant movement is always locomotion from one place to another.
questions.answer: False

questions.text: Consultant-generated application: A plant has healthy roots but xylem is blocked. Predict the first major transport problem.
questions.answer: Water and mineral salts will not move effectively from roots to leaves.
